plain_english: Life is not short. We just waste most of it. We spend our time on things that do not matter and then complain that we ran out of time. The problem is not how many years you get — it is how few of them you actually use.
original_excerpt: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 1

plain_english: You protect your money, your property, your possessions. But when it comes to your time, you are the most wasteful person alive. You give away hours to anyone who asks and never even notice they are gone.
original_excerpt: You are living as if destined to live forever. No thought of your frailty ever enters your head.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 3

plain_english: People spend their whole lives preparing to live. They put off everything important until later — and then later never comes. The biggest waste of life is postponement.
original_excerpt: The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 7 (attributed)
